title: Spurious early `finished` signal from AudioStreamPlayer3D
body:
### Tested versions

Only tested on Godot 4.3.stable.

### System information

Linux (current Gentoo), Godot 4.3.stable

### Issue description

I have a 3D scene and am adding positional audio.  The positional audio is added via script:

```gdscript
func shoot_sound(obj: Node) -> void:
    var p: AudioStreamPlayer3D = AudioStreamPlayer3D.new()
    p.bus = "Game"
    p.stream = preload("res://audio/shot.wav")
    p.script = preload("res://audio/3d_sound.gd")
    obj.add_child(p)
```
The script:
```gdscript
extends AudioStreamPlayer3D

func _ready() -> void:
    play()
    finished.connect(queue_free)
```
If I use this, the `finished` signal is fired ~24ms later, which kills the stream player before any sound is emitted.  If I instead modify my script:
```gdscript
extends AudioStreamPlayer3D

func _ready() -> void:
    play()
    finished.connect(_done)

func _done() -> void:
    if is_playing():
        print("Not done yet.")
    else:
        print("actually done.")
        queue_free()
```
This calls `_done()` _twice_, the first time after ~24ms, the second after sound playback is actually complete. The above code (with or without the printing) actually plays sound properly and deletes the node when complete properly, so `finished` seems to be triggering even when `is_playing()` is `true`.


### Steps to reproduce

- Create an `AudioStreamPlayer3D` in script as above.
- Note when `finished` triggers.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I just created a 3D scene that looked like:

```
SubViewportContainer
    SubViewport -- audio_listener_enable_3d set to true
        Camera3D
        Sprite3D
```

I used a simple script on the subvieportcontainer:

```gdscript
extends SubViewportContainer

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    var speed: float = 5.0 * delta
    var x: float = Input.get_axis("left", "right") * speed
    var z: float = Input.get_axis("up", "down") * speed
    $SubViewport/Sprite3D.position += Vector3(x, 0.0, z)
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("Fire"):
        shoot_sound($SubViewport/Sprite3D)
```
